problemText: Which group of words is a CLAUSE rather than a phrase?
choices: after the last ferry of the evening
the mechanic tightened the loose chain
hoping for a shorter line at the counter
to repair the cracked greenhouse panel
hints: A clause needs both a doer and an action; ask each option who is doing what.
An -ing word, a to-form, and a preposition all open phrases, not clauses.

problemText: Which group of words is a DEPENDENT clause?
choices: The greenhouse lost heat overnight
Unless the vents close automatically
Closing the vents before the first hard frost
in the greenhouse behind the cafeteria
hints: First keep only the options that have a real subject-verb pair.
Of those, check the front word: a subordinator such as unless, although, or because makes the clause dependent.

problemText: In the sentence "The custodian who repaired the flagpole left before anyone thanked him.", which group of words is the RELATIVE clause?
choices: The custodian who repaired the flagpole
before anyone thanked him
who repaired the flagpole
left before anyone thanked him
hints: A relative clause opens with who, whom, whose, which, or that and describes a noun.
One option is a dependent clause but opens with a subordinator instead of a relative pronoun, so it is not the relative clause.

problemText: Which of these is a complete sentence?
choices: The row of tall cedar hedges planted along the fence line by the previous owners.
Because the sprinkler timer reset itself at midnight every night that week.
Standing in the doorway with a clipboard and a list of every missing library book.
Rain flooded the courtyard.
hints: Length proves nothing. Hunt for a subject paired with a real main verb.
Two options never supply a main verb at all, and one has a subject-verb pair trapped behind a subordinator.

problemText: Which sentence contains a DEPENDENT CLAUSE rather than only phrases?
choices: Sorting the recycling after every assembly, the freshmen filled six bins.
The freshmen filled six bins with cans and cartons from the assembly.
After the assembly, the freshmen filled six bins.
After the assembly ended, the freshmen filled six bins.
hints: A dependent clause still needs its own subject-verb pair behind the subordinator.
The word after can open a prepositional phrase or a dependent clause; check whether a subject and verb follow it.

problemText: Which statement about this sentence is accurate? "The archivist, working alone in a basement room that flooded twice each spring, catalogued every donated letter before the grant expired."
choices: It contains two independent clauses.
It contains one independent clause and one dependent clause.
It contains one independent clause and two dependent clauses.
It contains no dependent clauses, only an independent clause and modifying phrases.
hints: Strip out the material set off by commas first, then see what remains as the main clause.
Count every subject-verb pair, including one opening with that and one opening with before; the commas are only fencing off a phrase with no subject at all.

problemText: Which sentence is a COMPOUND sentence?
choices: The ferry docked late, so the field trip skipped the museum.
The ferry docked late and unloaded its passengers in the rain.
Because the ferry docked late, the field trip skipped the museum.
The ferry, delayed by fog for nearly an hour, docked late.
hints: A compound sentence needs two independent clauses, so each side of the joining word must have its own subject.
One option has a single subject running two verbs, one opens with a subordinator, and one is a single clause wrapped around a modifying phrase.

problemText: What type of sentence is this? "When the power flickered in the west wing, the projector rebooted on its own."
choices: Simple
Compound
Complex
Compound-complex
hints: Count the independent clauses first, then the dependent ones.
One independent clause plus one dependent clause opening with a subordinator gets a specific name.

problemText: Which choice combines these into a correctly punctuated COMPOUND sentence? "The auction ended at nine. The last painting sold for twice its estimate."
choices: The auction ended at nine, the last painting sold for twice its estimate.
The auction ended at nine; the last painting sold for twice its estimate.
The auction ended at nine the last painting sold for twice its estimate.
When the auction ended at nine, the last painting sold for twice its estimate.
hints: Both halves are complete sentences, so the join has to be strong enough to hold them.
A comma alone is a splice and no mark at all is a run-on; a subordinator would make the sentence complex, not compound.

problemText: A writer wants to combine these two sentences so the reader remembers that the choir performed anyway: "The heater broke on the morning of the concert. The choir performed the whole program." Which combination does that best?
choices: The heater broke on the morning of the concert, the choir performed the whole program.
Although the choir performed the whole program, the heater broke on the morning of the concert.
The heater breaking on the morning of the concert and the choir performing the whole program without complaint.
Although the heater broke on the morning of the concert, the choir performed the whole program.
hints: The idea the reader should remember belongs in the independent clause; the background belongs in the dependent clause.
Rule out the option joined by a comma alone and the option with no main verb, then check which of the remaining two demotes the heater instead of the choir.

problemText: Which sentence is SIMPLE?
choices: The gallery opened at noon, and the line stretched down the block.
The gallery opened at noon and stayed crowded until closing.
Because the gallery opened at noon, the line stretched down the block.
The gallery opened at noon; the line stretched down the block.
hints: A simple sentence has exactly one independent clause and no dependent clause, however many verbs it carries.
Ask whether the words after and have their own subject. Two verbs sharing one subject is a compound verb, not a second clause.

problemText: What type of sentence is this? "The engineer who designed the footbridge inspected the cables every spring and replaced any strand that showed rust."
choices: Simple
Compound
Compound-complex
Complex
hints: Find the main subject, then decide whether the second verb has a subject of its own.
Both who designed the footbridge and that showed rust are dependent clauses, and inspected and replaced share the single subject engineer, so there is only one independent clause.

problemText: Which revision fixes the comma splice? "The oven timer never rang, the bread burned on the bottom."
choices: The oven timer never rang the bread burned on the bottom.
The oven timer never rang, so the bread burned on the bottom.
The oven timer never rang, the bread burned, on the bottom.
The oven timer never rang, therefore, the bread burned on the bottom.
hints: Two independent clauses need more than a comma: add a coordinating conjunction or a stronger mark.
Deleting the comma only makes a run-on, and therefore is not a coordinating conjunction, so a comma in front of it still leaves a splice.

problemText: Which of these is a FRAGMENT?
choices: The visiting coach protested for a full minute.
The referee waved off the goal, and the crowd groaned.
Which the visiting coach protested for a full minute after the whistle.
The crowd groaned.
hints: Read each option alone and ask whether you would send it by itself.
A subject-verb pair is not enough if a relative pronoun such as which sits in front of it.

problemText: Which revision fixes the run-on? "The delivery van blocked the alley all afternoon the shop owners called the city twice."
choices: The delivery van blocked the alley all afternoon; the shop owners called the city twice.
The delivery van blocked the alley all afternoon, the shop owners called the city twice.
The delivery van blocked the alley all afternoon, however, the shop owners called the city twice.
Because the delivery van blocked the alley all afternoon. The shop owners called the city twice.
hints: Both halves are independent clauses, so pick a join strong enough to stand between two complete thoughts.
Two of the wrong options trade the run-on for a comma splice, and the fourth trades it for a fragment.

problemText: Which version is punctuated correctly? "The rehearsal space was free on Tuesdays, therefore, the band booked it for the whole month."
choices: The rehearsal space was free on Tuesdays therefore the band booked it for the whole month.
The rehearsal space was free on Tuesdays, therefore the band booked it for the whole month.
The rehearsal space was free on Tuesdays; therefore, the band booked it for the whole month.
The rehearsal space was free on Tuesdays; therefore the band booked it, for the whole month.
hints: Therefore carries the meaning of a conjunction but not the grammar power of one.
A conjunctive adverb between two independent clauses takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

problemText: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: The night custodian, moving carefully between rows of drying canvases in the old art wing, switched off every light before eleven.
The night custodian switched off every light before eleven, the art wing stayed dark until morning.
The night custodian switched off every light before eleven the art wing stayed dark until morning.
Because the night custodian switched off every light before eleven. The art wing stayed dark until morning.
hints: Count independent clauses, not words. A long sentence with only one independent clause is never a run-on.
The three wrong options are a comma splice, a fused sentence, and a stranded dependent clause.

problemText: Which revision best fixes the error? "The tide pool held three kinds of anemone. Which the field guide never mentioned."
choices: The tide pool held three kinds of anemone, which the field guide never mentioned.
The tide pool held three kinds of anemone; which the field guide never mentioned.
The tide pool held three kinds of anemone, the field guide never mentioned them.
The tide pool held three kinds of anemone which the field guide never mentioned, it surprised the whole class.
hints: The second word group is a relative clause, so it must attach to the sentence it describes rather than stand alone.
A semicolon needs a complete sentence on its left AND on its right, and swapping in a comma between two independent clauses only creates a comma splice.

problemText: Which revision fixes the dangling modifier? "Rushing to finish before the bell, the diagram was left half-shaded."
choices: Rushing to finish before the bell, the diagram was left half-shaded by Priya.
Rushing to finish before the bell, Priya left the diagram half-shaded.
The diagram, rushing to finish before the bell, was left half-shaded.
Rushing to finish before the bell, half of the diagram was left shaded.
hints: Ask who is rushing, then check which option puts that person right after the comma.
Naming the true doer later in the sentence never repairs an opening modifier.

problemText: Which choice keeps the series parallel? "The training weekend taught the crew to read a tide chart, ___, and radio the harbor office."
choices: tying a bowline
how to tie a bowline
tie a bowline
to be tying a bowline
hints: Read the first and third items after taught the crew to and name the form they share.
Read a tide chart and radio the harbor office are both bare verbs following to, so the middle item must match.

problemText: Which revision places the modifier correctly? "The clerk handed the receipts to the auditor in a torn envelope."
choices: The clerk handed the receipts in a torn envelope to the auditor.
In a torn envelope, the clerk handed the receipts to the auditor.
The clerk handed the auditor the receipts and the torn envelope to be sorted.
The clerk in a torn envelope handed the receipts to the auditor.
hints: Decide what the torn envelope actually describes, then move the phrase next to that word.
Two options leave the phrase attached to a person, and one quietly changes what the sentence claims happened.

problemText: A writer wants to say that the shop repaired two of the bikes and no more than two. Which sentence says exactly that?
choices: The shop only repaired two of the bikes.
Only the shop repaired two of the bikes.
The shop repaired only two of the bikes.
The shop repaired two of the only bikes.
hints: A limiting word such as only belongs directly in front of the word it limits.
Placed before the verb it says repairing was all the shop did, and placed before the subject it says no one else repaired any.

problemText: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
choices: The grant will not only fund the new kiln but also it pays for the glazes.
The grant will not only fund the new kiln but also pay for the glazes.
The grant will not only fund the new kiln but also paying for the glazes.
Not only the grant will fund the new kiln but also the glazes for the ceramics room.
hints: The words after not only and after but also must match in grammatical form.
Test each half against the shared opener will: will fund works, so the second half needs a bare verb too.

problemText: Which sentence is written correctly?
choices: Balanced on a stepladder for nearly an hour, the banner was finally straightened by the two seniors.
The orientation packet explains where to park, how to find the office, and the schedule for the first week.
The orientation packet explains where to park, how to find the office, and when the first week begins.
Explaining where to park and how to find the office, the schedule for the first week is included in the orientation packet.
hints: Check two things in every option: does an opening modifier describe the noun right after the comma, and does every item in the list match in form?
Two options leave an opening phrase describing an object that cannot do the action, and one mixes two clauses with a plain noun phrase in the same series.
